title: The Number 1 Rule of Machine Learning and What Is Deep Learning Good For

cues.en: In the last video, we familiarized ourselves with Google's number one rule of machine learning, which is basically, if you don't need it, don't use it.
cues.zh: 上支影片認識了 Google 的機器學習第一條規則，基本上就是：如果不需要，就不要用。

cues.en: And with that in mind, what should we actually be looking to use, machine learning or deep learning for?
cues.zh: 記住這點，那究竟該把機器學習或深度學習用在哪裡？

cues.en: Well, problems with long lists of rules.
cues.zh: 需要很長一串規則的問題，

cues.en: So when the traditional approach fails, so remember, the traditional approach is you have some sort of data input.
cues.zh: 也就是傳統方法失效時。記得，傳統方法是先有某種資料輸入，

cues.en: You write a list of rules for that data to be manipulated in some way, shape or form.
cues.zh: 再寫一串規則，以某種方式處理資料，

cues.en: And then you have the outputs that you know.
cues.zh: 接著得到已知的輸出。

cues.en: But if you have a long, long list of rules, like the rules of driving a car, which could be hundreds, could be thousands, could be millions, who knows?
cues.zh: 但如果規則非常長，像開車的規則，可能有幾百、幾千、幾百萬條，誰知道呢？

cues.en: That's where machine learning and deep learning may help.
cues.zh: 這時機器學習與深度學習可能有幫助。

cues.en: And it kind of is at the moment in the world of self-driving cars, machine learning and deep learning are the state of the art approach continually changing environments.
cues.zh: 目前自駕車領域的確如此，機器學習與深度學習是最先進的方法。再來是持續改變的環境。

cues.en: So one of the benefits of deep learning is that it can keep learning if it needs to, and so it can adapt and learn to new scenarios.
cues.zh: 深度學習的一個優點，是有需要時可以持續學習，因此能適應、學習新情境。

cues.en: So if you update the data that your model was trained on, it can adjust to new, different kinds of data in the future.
cues.zh: 如果更新訓練模型用的資料，它就能調整，應對未來不同類型的新資料。

cues.en: So similarly to if you are driving a car, you might know your own neighborhood very well, but then when you go to somewhere you haven't been before, sure, you can draw on the foundations of what you
cues.zh: 就像開車，你可能很熟悉自己家附近，但到了沒去過的地方，當然可以運用

cues.en: know, but you're going to have to adapt.
cues.zh: 已有的基礎知識，不過還是得適應。

cues.en: How fast should you go?
cues.zh: 該開多快？

cues.en: Where should you stop?
cues.zh: 該在哪裡停下？

cues.en: Where should you park these kinds of things?
cues.zh: 該停在哪裡？像這些事情。

cues.en: So with problems with long list of rules or continually changing environments, or if you had a large, large data set.
cues.zh: 所以，規則很長的問題、持續改變的環境，或者你有一個非常大的資料集。

cues.en: And so this is where deep learning is flourishing in the world of technology.
cues.zh: 這正是深度學習在科技界蓬勃發展的地方。

cues.en: So let's give an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子，

cues.en: One of my favorites is the Food 101 data set, which you can search for online, which is images of 101 different kinds of foods.
cues.zh: 我很喜歡 Food-101 資料集，可以在線上搜尋，裡面有 101 種不同食物的影像。

cues.en: Now, we briefly looked at what a rule list might look like for cooking your grandmother's famous Sicilian roast chicken dish.
cues.zh: 我們簡單看過，要煮奶奶拿手的西西里烤雞，規則清單可能長什麼樣。

cues.en: But can you imagine if you wanted to build an app that could take photos of different food?
cues.zh: 但想像一下，如果要建立能拍攝不同食物的應用程式，

cues.en: How long your list of rules would be to differentiate 101 different foods There'd be so long, you need rule sets for every single one.
cues.zh: 為了分辨 101 種不同食物，規則會有多長？一定非常長，每種食物都需要自己的規則。

cues.en: Let's just take one food, for example.
cues.zh: 只看一種食物就好，

cues.en: How do you write a program to tell what a banana looks like?
cues.zh: 要怎麼寫程式，辨認香蕉長什麼樣？

cues.en: I mean, you'd have to code what a banana looks like.
cues.zh: 你得把香蕉的樣子寫進程式，

cues.en: But not only a banana.
cues.zh: 但不只是香蕉，

cues.en: What?
cues.zh: 還有，

cues.en: Everything that isn't a banana looks like.
cues.zh: 所有不是香蕉的東西長什麼樣。

cues.en: So keep this in mind.
cues.zh: 所以記住，

cues.en: What?
cues.zh: 什麼是

cues.en: Deep learning is good for Problems with long list of rules, continually changing environments, or discovering insights within large collections of data.
cues.zh: 深度學習擅長的：規則很長的問題、持續改變的環境，或者從大量資料集合中找出洞見。

cues.en: Now what?
cues.zh: 那什麼是

cues.en: Deep learning is not good for and I'm going to write typically here because again, this is problem specific.
cues.zh: 深度學習不擅長的？這裡我要加上「通常」，因為還是要看個別問題。

cues.en: Deep learning is quite powerful these days and things might change in the future.
cues.zh: 現今深度學習相當強大，未來也可能改變，

cues.en: So keep an open mind.
cues.zh: 所以保持開放心態。

cues.en: If there's anything about this course, It's not for me to tell you exactly what's what.
cues.zh: 這門課如果有個重點，不是我要告訴你每件事究竟是什麼，

cues.en: It's for me to spark a curiosity into you to figure out what's what, or even better yet, what's not what.
cues.zh: 而是激發你的好奇心，自己找出它是什麼，甚至更進一步，找出它不是什麼。

cues.en: So when you need explain ability as we'll see the patterns learned by a deep learning model, which is lots of numbers called weights and biases.
cues.zh: 第一，需要可解釋性時。之後會看到，深度學習模型學到的模式，是大量叫做權重與偏差的數字，

cues.en: We'll have a look at that later on.
cues.zh: 後面會再看看，

cues.en: I typically aren't interpretable by a human, so some of the times deep learning models can have a million, 10 million, 100 million, a billion.
cues.zh: 通常人類難以解讀。有時深度學習模型有一百萬、一千萬、一億、十億個，

cues.en: Some models are getting into the trillions of parameters.
cues.zh: 有些模型的參數量，已達兆的等級。

cues.en: When I say parameters, I mean numbers or patterns in data.
cues.zh: 我說參數，是指資料裡的數字或模式。

cues.en: Remember, machine learning is turning things into numbers and then writing a machine learning model to find patterns in those numbers.
cues.zh: 記住，機器學習是把東西轉成數字，再寫一個模型，找出數字裡的模式。

cues.en: So sometimes those patterns themselves can be lists of numbers that are in the millions.
cues.zh: 有時這些模式本身，就是數百萬個數字組成的清單。

cues.en: And so can you imagine looking at a list of numbers that has a million different things going on?
cues.zh: 想像看看，要查看有一百萬個不同內容的數字清單，

cues.en: It's going to be quite hard.
cues.zh: 會相當困難。

cues.en: I find it hard to understand three or four numbers, let alone a million.
cues.zh: 三、四個數字我都很難理解，更別說一百萬個。

cues.en: And when the traditional approach is a better option.
cues.zh: 第二，傳統方法是更好的選擇時。

cues.en: Again, this is Google's rule number one of machine learning.
cues.zh: 這又是 Google 的機器學習第一條規則，

cues.en: If you can do what you need to do with a simple rule based system, well, maybe you don't need to use machine learning.
cues.zh: 如果用簡單的規則式系統，就能完成需要的事情，也許就不需要機器學習，

cues.en: Or deep learning.
cues.zh: 或深度學習。

cues.en: Again, I'm going to use the deep learning and machine learning terms interchangeably.
cues.zh: 再說一次，我會交替使用深度學習與機器學習這兩個詞，

cues.en: I'm not too concerned with definitions.
cues.zh: 不太拘泥於定義。

cues.en: You can form your own definitions, but just so you know, from my perspective, ML and deep learning are quite similar when errors are unacceptable.
cues.zh: 你可以形成自己的定義，但讓你知道，從我的角度，ML 與深度學習很相近。再來是無法接受錯誤時。

cues.en: So since the outputs of a deep learning model aren't always predictable, we'll see that deep learning models are probabilistic.
cues.zh: 因為深度學習模型的輸出不一定總可預測，我們會看到它們具有機率性，

cues.en: That means they're when they predict something, they're making a probabilistic bet on it.
cues.zh: 表示在預測某件事時，是根據機率下判斷。

cues.en: Whereas in a rule based system, you kind of know what the outputs are going to be every single time.
cues.zh: 規則式系統則大致能知道，每次的輸出會是什麼。

cues.en: So if you can't have errors based on probabilistic errors, well then you probably shouldn't use deep learning.
cues.zh: 所以如果無法接受由機率產生的錯誤，大概就不應該使用深度學習，

cues.en: And you'd like to go back to a simple rule based system.
cues.zh: 而是回到簡單的規則式系統。

cues.en: And then finally, when you don't have much data.
cues.zh: 最後，當你沒有很多資料時。

cues.en: So deep learning models usually require a fairly large amount of data to produce great results.
cues.zh: 深度學習模型通常需要相當大量的資料，才能產生很好的結果。

cues.en: However, there's a caveat here.
cues.zh: 不過這裡有但書。

cues.en: You know, at the start I said typically we're going to see some techniques of how to get great results without huge amounts of data.
cues.zh: 開頭說過是「通常」，我們會看到一些不用大量資料也能取得好結果的技巧。

cues.en: And again, I wrote typically here because there are techniques you can just research, deep learning explainability, you're going to find a whole bunch of stuff.
cues.zh: 我在這裡寫「通常」，也是因為有其他技術。可以研究深度學習可解釋性，會找到很多內容。

cues.en: You can look up examples of when machine learning versus deep learning and then when errors are unacceptable.
cues.zh: 可以查機器學習與深度學習的比較例子，以及無法接受錯誤時怎麼處理。

cues.en: Again, there are ways to make your model reproducible, so it predicts you know what's going to come out.
cues.zh: 同樣地，也有辦法讓模型可重現，讓你知道會預測出什麼。

cues.zh: 我們也會做很多測試，驗證這一點。
